## Introduction




## What is this tool?

This ecosystem assessment tool from the [ECOsystem and Conservation Assessment Tools (EcoCAT)](https://www.kew.org/science/our-science/projects/EcoCAT "url link to the RBG Kew EcoCAT project webpage"){target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer"} can be used to upload maps and assess the changes and extent of ecosystems. The tool follows the [IUCN Red List of Ecosystem assessment guidelines](https://portals.iucn.org/library/sites/library/files/documents/2024-021-En.pdf "pdf file of the RLE ecosytem assessment guidelines"){target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer"} to generate ecosystem metrics. The user can then use this tool to down load reports, assessment data, maps and figures to be used in any additional work such as for offical reports and publications. 

The ecosystem assessment tool can help provide standardised ecosystem assessments, to ensure ecosystem status are comparable across all assessed ecosystems at a global scale. 


## What is an ecosytem risk assessement?



## Who is this tool for?

This ecosystem assessment tool has been built to help anyone implementing an IUCN Red List of Ecosystem assessment. It has been designed for users who already have a map(s) of an ecosystem that they would like to perform an ecosystem assessment on following the [IUCN Red List of Ecosystem assessment guidelines](https://portals.iucn.org/library/sites/library/files/documents/2024-021-En.pdf "pdf file of the RLE ecosytem assessment guidelines"){target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer"}.

## What can this tool do?

This tool can currently generate the following information from mapped ecosystems:

-   Descriptive information of a mapped ecosystem

-   Criterion A (temporal change) - only when \>1 time period of data is uploaded

-   Criterion B (Area and extent of occurrence)
